version.value: First movement only, for soprano and an orchestra of cellos, in the form of 1938; sung in Portuguese.
version.note: The Columbia labels give the movement as “Aria – Cantilena”, in two parts marked “Beginning” and “Conclusion”, and read “Sung in Portuguese”. The Dansa (Martelo) was added in 1945 and is not on this disc.

value.name: Eight cellos and double bass (players not named)

performers.note: Both label scans read “BIDÚ SAYÃO (Soprano) with Eight ’Celli and Bass conducted by Heitor Villa-Lobos; Solo ’Cello: Leonard Rose”. The Internet Archive description gives the same names.

date.note: The Internet Archive item dates the recording 1945. The record appears in the Columbia catalogue of 1946, and a New Yorker profile places Villa-Lobos in New York in February 1945. No session date is stated in the sources consulted.

place.note: No recording location is stated on the labels or in the Internet Archive description.

label.note: The labels read “Columbia Masterworks … Made in U.S.A.”.

catalogue.value: 71670-D, 12-inch 78 rpm; listed in the Columbia catalogues of 1946 and 1947
catalogue.note: The 1946 catalogue lists “Bachiana Brasileira No. 5 (Villa-Lobos)” with Bidú Sayão and an orchestra conducted by Villa-Lobos at 71670-D; the 1947 catalogue lists it at the same number with a price of 1.00.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side one, “(Beginning)”: XCO 34194; side two, “(Conclusion)”: XCO 34195. Take numbers are not shown.
matrixTakeSides.note: Read from the two label scans in the Internet Archive item.

credits.note: The item was uploaded by a private account in the Internet Archive’s hifidelity collection. No transfer engineer is named, and the account name is not reproduced here.

date.note: The item’s public date, 10 March 2025, is the date of upload, not of the transfer.

processing.value: Per the uploader: equalisation with a 300 Hz bass turnover and a treble roll-off, and de-clicking with iZotope RX10; the original file is a WAV and the site’s stream is the Internet Archive MP3 derivative.
processing.note: The two disc sides are run together in one file. The source disc copy and the playback equipment are not described.

digital.format: Internet Archive derivative VBR MP3 from an uploaded WAV; one file for both disc sides

composition.value: Villa-Lobos died in 1959, so the work is in copyright in the EU, under the life-plus-70 term, until the end of 2029. IMSLP records it as public domain in Canada and in life-plus-50 countries and as probably still protected in the United States; its first publication was in 1947 (Associated Music Publishers).
composition.note: Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. This dossier does not assert that the composition is free of copyright.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963 (Columbia 71670-D, listed in the 1946 catalogue).
recording.note: The 1946 catalogue is a dated witness that the disc was on sale by then; the exact release date is not established. The Internet Archive item carries a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 label chosen by the uploader, which is not relied on here. The United States status of a recording first published in 1945 or 1946 is not established.

rights.creditLine: Heitor Villa-Lobos, Bachianas Brasileiras No. 5, I. Ária (Cantilena). Bidú Sayão, soprano; Leonard Rose, solo cello; eight cellos and double bass; Heitor Villa-Lobos, conductor. Columbia Masterworks 71670-D (matrices XCO 34194–34195), recorded 1945, issued by 1946. Internet Archive item bachianas-brasileiras-no.-5 (uploader’s transfer). Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established.
